method: Independent source-led rebuilding of the 40 questions; no automatic first-eight truncation. Search-index excerpts are explicitly distinguished from full page text. Cambridge direct opens returned 403; its actual indexed dictionary definitions were reviewed, not corpus examples.

tierRationale.200: Familiar everyday garments, tools and materials.
tierRationale.400: Common named fabrics, a traditional garment, accessories and beauty vocabulary.
tierRationale.600: Named cuts, processes and products familiar to enthusiasts.
tierRationale.800: More specialized materials and craft terminology.
tierRationale.1000: Textile finishing, historic footwear, cutting and jewelry techniques.

retiredPolicy: All 240 original IDs replaced by the approved 901–908 range; the shared retired registry is owned by integration.

corrections.issue: Jasmine question accepted الفل indiscriminately and used broad flowering/geographical clues; omitted.
الحقيبة الكبيرة was a vague synonym for suitcase; omitted.
Generic البليد and كاروهات were overbroad aliases for tartan; omitted.
Burnt sienna is not interchangeable with unqualified sienna; omitted.
Organza re-reviewed and moved to 600 by answer familiarity, rather than keeping inflated legacy tier.

items.evidence: Dictionary definition: wool is the soft thick hair of sheep and some other animals.
Dictionary definition identifies silk as cloth or thread produced by silkworms.
Dictionary defines jeans as informal trousers made from denim.
Dictionary defines a sandal as a light shoe whose sole is held by straps.
Dictionary identifies the cosmetic used to darken, thicken and lengthen eyelashes.
Dictionary definition: a circular piece of jewelry worn on a finger.
Dictionary specifies a pointed metal sewing tool with a hole for thread.
Dictionary defines a model as a person wearing clothing to be photographed or shown to buyers.
Dictionary defines velvet as fabric with a thick soft surface; Arabic equivalent reviewed editorially.
Dictionary distinguishes the smooth shiny face from the non-shiny reverse.
Dictionary identifies the long loose Japanese garment with very wide sleeves.
Dictionary defines a small flat bag without a handle, used especially on formal occasions.
Sections What Is Concealer and Difference describe targeted coverage, versus whole-face foundation.
GIA Natural Pearls describes formation inside mollusks; earlier paragraph describes necklaces.
Dictionary defines decorating cloth with patterns or pictures sewn onto it.
English dictionary definition describes a long narrow stage used by fashion models.
American Heritage defines sheer stiff silk/synthetic fabric used in evening dresses.
Introduction identifies cashmere as goat undercoat; distinguishes it from Angora-goat mohair.
Dictionary describes a knitted upper garment fastened at the front with buttons.
Dictionary identifies the narrow high heel; accepted Arabic transliterations reviewed.
Introduction and application steps establish primer before foundation and longer makeup wear.
GIA defines a metric carat as 200 milligrams.
Dictionary describes decorative fabric pieces sewn or fixed onto other fabric.
Dictionary describes handmade expensive clothing, especially for individual customers in Paris fashion houses.
Introduction and Production explicitly identify Angora goats as the source of mohair.
About the fiber identifies regenerated cellulose, wood pulp and closed-loop solvent recovery for TENCEL Lyocell.
Dictionary defines decorative material attached around the waist; Getty corroborates short skirtlike extension.
Dictionary defines strong cloth shoes with rope soles.
Color Correcting Primer section states that green tint counteracts redness.
Cabochons: Simple and Double identifies the simple form as rounded top and flat bottom.
Dictionary defines tight folds held with decorative stitches; not generic gathering or elastic shirring.
Dictionary defines clothes produced in standard sizes, rather than to fit an individual.
CottonWorks specifies concentrated caustic soda under tension, increased dye affinity and luster.
Dictionary describes light cloth with alternating raised and flat strips.
FIT definition gives shoulder fullness, fitted wrist and gigot synonym; details explain French leg-of-lamb name.
FIT defines high platform shoes mostly worn in Venice during the 16th and 17th centuries.
L’Oreal explains name from strobe lights, highlighting alone, and contrast with contouring.
Filigree and Granulation section defines soldered fine wires and the resulting lace-like openwork.
V&A describes Vionnet championing bias cutting across the grain for draping that follows the body.
Met entry credits Elsa Schiaparelli and describes hand-knit sweaters and the reputation-making trompe-l’oeil bowknot; wording avoids claiming paint.
